title: Quality of life in patients undergoing treatment for chronic graft-versus-host disease depending on extracorporeal photopheresis
summary:
Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGvHD) is a common complication following allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and is associated with increased mortality and morbidity. The multitude of possible symptoms and the unpredictability of the course of the disease mean that affected patients remain in their sick role for a long time and face an uncertain future (de Vere Hunt et al., 2021). High psychological stress and a significant loss of quality of life are therefore further consequences of cGvHD. In addition to reducing the burden of physical symptoms, improving patients' quality of life should therefore also be a therapeutic goal. Alongside drug therapy, extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) is an important pillar of treatment and is used when first-line therapy with steroids is not sufficient. In everyday clinical practice, patients report an improvement in their quality of life during ECP, regardless of the standardised criteria used to diagnose and assess the severity of cGvHD. 
Given the relevance of patient-reported endpoints and the rudimentary data available on quality of life in patients with cGvHD and ECP, this study aims to shed more light on this field and lay the foundation for future research projects.

interventions.name: Group 1: includes all patients with cGvHD already undergoing ECP treatment, one-time data collection (cross-section)
Group 2: includes all patients with cGvHD scheduled for ECP treatment, multiple data collection (3-4 times) over 6 months (longitudinal)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group 1 (cross-sectional study):
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Ongoing ECP therapy for cGvHD
- Complete remission of the underlying haematological disease or molecular persistence of disease markers without increasing dynamics
- Independent response to the items (assistance from a typist is possible, but the patient must have a linguistic and conceptual understanding)

Group 2 (longitudinal study):
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Patients for whom ECP therapy is indicated as a treatment option (e.g. in steroid-refractory cGvHD)
- Complete remission of the underlying haematological disease or molecular persistence of disease markers without increasing dynamics
- Independent response to the items (assistance from a typist is possible, but the patient must have a linguistic and conceptual understanding)
Exclusion criteria:
Group 1 (cross-sectional study):
- Lack of/withdrawn consent
- Requirements for study participation cannot be met (impaired intelligence, care needs, poor German language skills, severe psychiatric/neurological disease)
- Uncontrolled infection at inclusion
- Overlap syndrome with signs of acute and chronic GvHD

Group 2 (longitudinal study):
- Lack of/withdrawn consent
- Requirements for study participation cannot be met (impaired intelligence, care needs, poor German language skills, severe psychiatric/neurological disease)
- Uncontrolled infection at inclusion
- Overlap syndrome with signs of acute and chronic GvHD
- Contraindications to ECP treatment
